findings.quote: the answer that Agesipolis and his colleagues had obtained
findings.problem: Greek has οἱ περὶ τὸν Ἁγέπολιν: the Rhodian envoy Hagepolis, not Agesipolis (a different name, Spartan).
findings.proposed_fix: the answer that Hagepolis and his colleagues had obtained

units.note: Name-form only; rest of chapter matches the Greek (Antonius tribune, Philophron before Astymedes, reply sense, correlatives all fine).

findings.quote: but that by giving special weight and dignity to the move they hoped to strip away the suspicions
findings.problem: Greek: ἀλλὰ βουλόμενοι κατὰ τὴν ὑπέρθεσιν τῆς ἐπιβολῆς ἀφαιρεῖσθαι τὰς ὑπονοίας. ὑπέρθεσις means putting off, postponement, delay; nothing in it says 'special weight and dignity'. Sense: by the deferral of their undertaking (the alliance proposal) they hoped to remove suspicions.
findings.proposed_fix: but that by postponing the proposal they hoped to strip away the suspicions

units.note: Number checks passed: 140 years (ἔτη τετταράκοντα πρὸς τοῖς ἑκατόν), 10,000 gold pieces (μυρίων χρυσῶν). The Greek here is somewhat compressed; the rendering of ὑπέρθεσις is the only point of doubt.

Minor, not flagged: διάληψις is 'judgment/assessment', English says 'conduct', and πρότερον ἐπιστήσαντες could be 'first drawing attention' rather than 'already'. This is an excerptor's fragment of uncertain construction; sense is not inverted.

findings.quote: The most prominent of these were Hippocrates and his brother Diomedon among the Coans, and Deinon and Polyaratus among the Rhodians.
findings.problem: Greek breaks off mid-word: τούτων δ᾽ ἦσαν ἐπιφανέστατοι παρὰ μὲν τοῖς Κῴοις Ἱππόκριτος καὶ Διομέδων ἀδελ[...]. The text ends at ἀδελ- (presumably ἀδελφοί); the Rhodian names Deinon and Polyaratus are NOT in the Greek and are silently supplied, so the English reads as whole.
findings.proposed_fix: The most prominent of these among the Coans were Hippocrates and Diomedon, brothers [the text breaks off here].

findings.quote: and in the end they disappointed all expectations.
findings.problem: Greek: καὶ πάσας ἐξήλεγχον τὰς ἐλπίδας, 'and they put every hope to the test' (they tried every resource), not 'disappointed all expectations'. The verb is ἐξελέγχω (examine, test, prove); the English reverses the sense to failure.
findings.proposed_fix: and they put every hope to the test.

units.note: The ending is a truncation of the Greek text (the next chapter's Greek is not in this unit); Rhodian names appear to be supplied from context (compare later chapters naming Deinon and Polyaratus).
